the immunohistochemical expression and subcellular location of β‐catenins, E‐cadhereins, cyclin Ds and c‐mycs in benign trichogenetic tumors.
the role of βcatenin, Ecadherin, cmyc and cyclin D1 in benign trichogeneous tumors.
the role of the Wnt/β‐catenin pathway in benign trichogenous neoplasms.

β‐catenin and its related proteins are not useful for differential diagnosis of benign trichogenic skin tumors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of c‐myc and cyclin D1 in benign trichogeneic tumors is not associated with nuclear β‐catenin expression.
β‐catenin is not only a component of the cytoskeletal adhesion molecules but also plays a role in the regulation of cell growth, differentiation and apoptosis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of these proteins is not limited to PMXs and may also be seen in benign hair tumors.
the expression of β-catenin is a very useful diagnostic marker for differentiating PMX from other benign trichogenic tumours.
